4c69d03f511c8931:MSFT-NCT07299019.summary: Only the headline is available. It says a phase 2 orelabrutinib study in relapsing-remitting MS showed promising efficacy. No trial identifier, measure, data or primary outcome is given in the text.

4c69d03f511c8931:MSFT-NCT04711148.summary: The headline says orelabrutinib showed promising efficacy in a phase 2 study in relapsing-remitting MS. The text given has no data, main measure, or safety details, so no main goal can be confirmed as met.

68c5d9e8a4719912:MSFT-NCT06053749.summary: The announcement reports Phase 2 results for foralumab in nonactive SPMS in a trial called INFORM-MS (NCT06292923), which is a different trial from the interferon beta trial named. It reports no results for this trial.

6d62f11c1c4c4292:MSFT-2017-000426-35.summary: The text describes a large Swedish study linking rituximab, used off label for MS, to a higher risk of inflammatory bowel disease, particularly Crohn's disease. It does not mention the Low-dose Rituximab in MS trial or report its results.

75e2846265d82a99:MSFT-NCT07762040.summary: The text is only a headline saying orelabrutinib reduced brain lesions in RRMS by 90% in a Phase 2 trial. It gives no trial identifier, design or other details, so it cannot be tied to MSFT-NCT07762040.

8bc19c6222104574:MSFT-NCT06846281.summary: The text gives only a headline mentioning remibrutinib Phase 3 results in relapsing MS. It names no trial, gives no outcomes, and does not say whether the main goal was met.

acfa17cd22d3f09b:MSFT-NCT07762040.summary: The text is a general podcast episode description about disease modifying drugs in MS. It does not mention this trial or report any trial results.

ccfbb66d31ee307e:MSFT-NCT05054140.summary: The title says vidofludimus calcium reduced the risk of disability worsening by 30% in people with primary progressive MS in the Phase 2 CALLIPER trial. The text gives no detail on the primary endpoint, statistical significance or safety.

e300af6c6f7f8276:MSFT-2017-000426-35.summary: The text contains only a title and the journal name. It reports no results, no outcome measures and no mention of the Low-dose Rituximab in MS trial, so nothing about this trial can be determined.

e300af6c6f7f8276:MSFT-NCT03002038.summary: The text contains only a title and the journal name. It reports no results, endpoints, or safety findings, and it does not mention this trial or its azathioprine and rituximab comparison in NMOSD.

e300af6c6f7f8276:MSFT-NCT00787722.summary: The text gives only a title about rituximab in multiple sclerosis and neuromyelitis optica spectrum disorder. It reports no trial results, no named trial, and no details about this trial.

f5815cad7cae3e07:MSFT-2025-523892-50-00.summary: The text is a systematic review and meta-analysis of tolebrutinib in MS, pooling four publications (three reporting four randomized trials, plus one extension study). It does not name or report results specific to MSBenefiT.

f5815cad7cae3e07:MSFT-NCT04742400.measure: Disability progression, MRI activity, brain volume, safety outcomes
f5815cad7cae3e07:MSFT-NCT04742400.summary: This systematic review and meta-analysis pooled four randomized trials and one extension study of tolebrutinib. It reports reduced confirmed disability progression risk at ≥3 and ≥6 months, with disability improvement numerically higher but not conclusive. It does not report results for this specific trial.

AAN2026-000844:MSFT-NCT04411641:MSFT-NCT.measure: Subgroup analyses of disability accumulation and annualized relapse rate
AAN2026-000844:MSFT-NCT04411641:MSFT-NCT.summary: All pre-specified subgroups favored tolebrutinib over placebo, with some differences in effect size. Adjusted annualized adjudicated relapse rate was low in both groups (0.033 tolebrutinib, 0.032 placebo). Effect on disability accumulation was overall consistent across subgroups.

AAN2026-001923:MSFT-NCT04201262:MSFT-NCT.measure: Adjudicated on-trial relapse (OTR) risk reduction vs placebo
AAN2026-001923:MSFT-NCT04201262:MSFT-NCT.summary: In the final CHAMPION-NMOSD analysis, no patient on ravulizumab had an adjudicated relapse, a 98.9% relapse risk reduction vs placebo. Most patients had stable or improved disability. Safety was consistent with prior analyses, with one cardiovascular death unrelated to ravulizumab.

AAN2026-002005:MSFT-NCT05232825:MSFT-NCT.measure: Week 96 MRI and relapse activity, EDSS, and safety of subcutaneous ocrelizumab
AAN2026-002005:MSFT-NCT05232825:MSFT-NCT.summary: At week 96, 96.7% of patients were relapse free and annualized relapse rate was 0.02 and 0.03 across arms. EDSS stayed stable. 86.3% had an adverse event, 5.2% a serious one; no treatment-emergent ADA to ocrelizumab were reported.

AAN2026-002026:MSFT-NCT01194570:MSFT-NCT.summary: The announcement reports the primary analysis of ORATORIO-HAND, a separate ocrelizumab vs placebo study in primary progressive MS (505 vs 508 patients). It does not report results for the Oratorio trial MSFT-NCT01194570.

AAN2026-002026:MSFT-NCT04035005:MSFT-NCT.summary: Ocrelizumab beat placebo on 12W-cCDP (32.7% vs 40.4%; HR 0.70; P=0.0007), with benefits on 9HPT and EDSS components. Safety was similar between arms, apart from more infusion-related reactions with ocrelizumab (20.8% vs 4.3%).

AAN2026-002137:MSFT-NCT01480076:MSFT-NCT.summary: The announcement describes a different study also called ENABLE, a phase four observational study of ublituximab in relapsing MS. It does not mention dalfampridine, so it reports no results for the named trial.

AAN2026-002137:MSFT-NCT06433752:MSFT-NCT.measure: Real-world disease control, safety and infusion-related reactions with ublituximab
AAN2026-002137:MSFT-NCT06433752:MSFT-NCT.summary: In ENABLE's real-world cohort, on-treatment annualized relapse rate was 0.015 and 99.5% stayed relapse-free. First-dose infusion-related reactions occurred in 17.3%, and TSQM and MSIS-29 scores improved at Day 15 and week 24. The study is ongoing.

AAN2026-002771:MSFT-NCT04075266:MSFT-NCT.summary: Ocrelizumab was noninferior to fingolimod for relapse control in pediatric-onset relapsing-remitting MS and superior on new/enlarging T2 and T1 Gd+ lesions. Infusion reactions, mostly mild or moderate, occurred in 48.4%, and no adverse event led to withdrawal.

AAN2026-002771:MSFT-NCT05123703:MSFT-NCT.measure: Relapse rate (noninferiority) vs fingolimod; new/enlarging T2 lesions
AAN2026-002771:MSFT-NCT05123703:MSFT-NCT.summary: Ocrelizumab was noninferior to fingolimod on relapse control (RR 0.52; 95% CI 0.19-1.33) and superior on new/enlarging T2 lesions (RR 0.52) and T1 Gd+ lesions at Week 12 (RR 0.13). It was well tolerated; no adverse events led to withdrawal.

AAN2026-002798:MSFT-NCT04998812:MSFT-NCT.measure: Infant B-cell levels and vaccine responses at Month 13 after possible ocrelizumab exposure
AAN2026-002798:MSFT-NCT04998812:MSFT-NCT.summary: In MINORE, 92.8% of infants (26/28) had normal B-cell levels at Month 13. Infants showed positive vaccine responses, most had normal growth and development, and no new safety signals were seen. Results are reported together with SOPRANINO.

AAN2026-002798:MSFT-NCT04998851:MSFT-NCT.measure: Infant B-cell levels and vaccine humoral responses at Month 13
AAN2026-002798:MSFT-NCT04998851:MSFT-NCT.summary: In SOPRANINO, 11 mother-infant pairs (84.6%) completed the study. At Month 13, all 11 infants had normal B-cell levels, and vaccine responses were positive. No new safety signals were seen in infants, and infections were as expected.

AAN2026-002813:MSFT-NCT04544449:MSFT-NCT.summary: The announcement describes baseline characteristics of 985 PPMS patients enrolled in FENtrepid, comparing fenebrutinib with ocrelizumab. It states primary efficacy and safety results will be presented, but reports none.

AAN2026-002813:MSFT-NCT05119569:MSFT-NCT.summary: The text describes FENtrepid, a trial in primary progressive MS, not FENopta. It reports only baseline characteristics of 985 patients and says primary efficacy and safety results will be presented.

AAN2026-002827:MSFT-NCT04879628:MSFT-NCT.measure: Gd+ T1 lesions at week 144 (open-label extension)
AAN2026-002827:MSFT-NCT04879628:MSFT-NCT.summary: In the 3-year open-label extension, 78% of participants (100) stayed on treatment. Gd+ T1 and new/enlarging T2 lesion counts stayed low, 86% of the original 1200mg IV arm were relapse-free, and no new safety signals appeared.

AAN2026-002869:MSFT-NCT04879628:MSFT-NCT.measure: Plasma NfL, CXCL13 and brain volume loss to week 144
AAN2026-002869:MSFT-NCT04879628:MSFT-NCT.summary: From baseline to week 144, plasma NfL fell 35–49% and CXCL13 fell 28–61% across the arms. In the IV arm, median brain volume loss was -0.84% for whole brain, -1.18% for thalamus and -0.85% for cortex.

AAN2026-002870:MSFT-NCT04410978:MSFT-NCT.measure: Blood levels of leukocytes, lymphocytes, neutrophils, monocytes, IgG, IgM and platelets
AAN2026-002870:MSFT-NCT04410978:MSFT-NCT.summary: Pooled analysis of the HERCULES and GEMINI trials over 42 months found mean immune cell counts, immunoglobulins and platelets stayed stable and within normal ranges with tolebrutinib, placebo and teriflunomide. The text states no depletion of leukocytes, immunoglobulins or platelets.

AAN2026-002870:MSFT-NCT04410991:MSFT-NCT.measure: Blood levels of leukocytes, lymphocytes, neutrophils, monocytes, IgG, IgM and platelets
AAN2026-002870:MSFT-NCT04410991:MSFT-NCT.summary: Over 42 months, mean immune cell counts, immunoglobulin levels and platelet counts stayed stable and within normal ranges with tolebrutinib, placebo and teriflunomide. The text says tolebrutinib did not deplete circulating leukocytes, immunoglobulins or platelets.

AAN2026-002870:MSFT-NCT04411641:MSFT-NCT.measure: Blood levels of immune cells, immunoglobulins, and platelets
AAN2026-002870:MSFT-NCT04411641:MSFT-NCT.summary: Over 42 months in HERCULES and GEMINI, mean leukocyte, lymphocyte, neutrophil, monocyte, IgG, IgM and platelet levels stayed within normal ranges with tolebrutinib, placebo and teriflunomide. The authors say tolebrutinib did not deplete these.

AAN2026-002878:MSFT-NCT04411641:MSFT-NCT.measure: Time to onset of 6-month confirmed disability progression (CDP)
AAN2026-002878:MSFT-NCT04411641:MSFT-NCT.summary: In a North American subgroup analysis, tolebrutinib delayed 6-month CDP versus placebo (HR 0.46 North America, 0.38 US, 0.69 overall). The authors note the small subgroup sample sizes as a limitation.

AAN2026-002881:MSFT-NCT04458051:MSFT-NCT.summary: The announcement describes baseline characteristics of 767 PERSEUS participants with PPMS (mean age 45.3, mean EDSS 4.9). Efficacy and safety results are only said to be forthcoming at AAN; none are reported.

AAN2026-002896:MSFT-NCT06141473:MSFT-NCT.measure: Usability of smartphone video AI motor function assessments
AAN2026-002896:MSFT-NCT06141473:MSFT-NCT.summary: Human factors results showed high overall usability scores (8.3/10). Baseline video AI-based assessment results will be shared later, and the main results are expected at study completion.

AAN2026-002896:MSFT-NCT06141486:MSFT-NCT.measure: Usability of smartphone video AI assessments of motor function
AAN2026-002896:MSFT-NCT06141486:MSFT-NCT.summary: The text reports a high overall usability score (8.3/10) for the smartphone video assessment method in a substudy covering RMS and nrSPMS. Baseline results and main results are still to come. It does not name FREVIVA or report trial outcomes.

AAN2026-003589:MSFT-NCT03085810:MSFT-NCT.measure: Preservation of ambulation (T25FW) and hand function (9HPT) at healthy-control levels
AAN2026-003589:MSFT-NCT03085810:MSFT-NCT.summary: At 6 years in ENSEMBLE (616 patients), 82.2% had no worsening of ambulation and 93.5% none in hand function. 45.7% with baseline walking impairment and 55.2% with baseline hand dysfunction improved to healthy-control levels.

AAN2026-003589:MSFT-NCT03599245:MSFT-NCT.measure: Ambulation (T25FW) and hand function (9HPT) relative to healthy-control levels over 6 years
AAN2026-003589:MSFT-NCT03599245:MSFT-NCT.summary: In 616 patients on first-line ocrelizumab, 82.2% had no worsening of ambulation and 93.5% none in hand function after 6 years. About half of those with baseline impairment improved to healthy-control levels (45.7% walking, 55.2% hand function).

AAN2026-003727:MSFT-NCT03838770:MSFT-NCT.summary: These are secondary outcomes. The active tDCS plus cognitive training group improved significantly on DET (p=.006) and ONB (p=.013), with trends on IDN and ONB accuracy. The sham group showed no significant changes.

AAN2026-004258:MSFT-2005-006071-12:MSFT-.summary: The announcement covers ADVANCE-CIDP1 and ADVANCE-CIDP3, trials of fSCIG in CIDP, not the MS trial named (levoleucovorin in relapsing MS). It reports mostly mild/moderate local adverse events, which tended to decrease over time.

AAN2026-004258:MSFT-NCT00906399:MSFT-NCT.summary: The text covers ADVANCE-CIDP1 and ADVANCE-CIDP3, trials of fSCIG in CIDP, not the MS trial ADVANCE of peginterferon beta-1a. It reports nothing about the named MS trial.

AAN2026-005945:MSFT-NCT04586010:MSFT-NCT.summary: The announcement gives baseline characteristics for 1497 enrolled patients (mean age 35.8 years, mean EDSS 2.5). It says primary efficacy and safety data will be presented, but reports no outcome results.

AAN2026-005945:MSFT-NCT04586023:MSFT-NCT.summary: The text gives baseline characteristics for 1497 enrolled patients across the FENhance studies and says primary efficacy and safety data will be presented. It reports no efficacy or safety results for FENhance 2.

AAN2026-005945:MSFT-NCT05119569:MSFT-NCT.summary: The announcement concerns the FENhance 1 and 2 studies of fenebrutinib vs teriflunomide, not FENopta. It gives baseline characteristics of 1497 enrolled patients and says primary efficacy and safety data will be presented. No results are reported.

AAN2026-006020:MSFT-NCT05271409:MSFT-NCT.summary: In 132 patients, satralizumab prolonged time to first relapse versus placebo, with a 68% lower relapse risk (HR 0.32, p=0.0025). Key secondary endpoints were also significant. Adverse event and infection rates were comparable between groups.

361fca5d8825afd7:MSFT-NCT06053749.summary: The text is only a headline saying Tiziana Life Sciences reported positive Phase 2a INFORM-MS results for intranasal foralumab. It gives no data or measures, and it concerns a different medicine from the interferon beta products in this trial.

785f502bbb687fbc:MSFT-NCT06053749.summary: Tiziana is hosting an investor call on what it calls positive Phase 2a INFORM-MS topline results. The text gives no data, no main measure, and no mention of interferon beta products, so it cannot be tied to this trial.
